generated_by: hand-authored during production; every entry is added by the run that first verified the source
what_this_is: The lane-neutral registry of FIRST-HAND and OFFICIAL sources MIW has verified and intends to reuse. Oral, Written, Notes and Study production all read it. It exists so that a primary source is researched ONCE, verified, preserved, reused, and revalidated when due - rather than rediscovered from the open web on every production run.
what_this_is_not: NOT answer authority by itself. Authority derives from ISSUER + VERSION + APPLICABILITY + CURRENTNESS, never from the fact that a file or a record exists locally. A cached entry marked CURRENT_VERIFIED still gets a lightweight supersession check before it is relied on for a current/latest claim.
why_it_exists: Recorded from a real production failure. The H1 BMP MS card was authored from a currency record that was itself one edition out of date, because the original check asked 'does BMP MS supersede BMP5?' - a question that returns the launch coverage, answers correctly, and is structurally incapable of revealing that a later edition has since appeared. See query_discipline below.

query_discipline.required: What has the authoritative publisher said MOST RECENTLY about this publication or instrument?
query_discipline.rule: Both questions must be asked. The first establishes the transition; only the second establishes the present state. A correct historical transition plus a stale present state reads exactly like current truth and is the failure this registry exists to prevent.

conventions.bytes_storage: Downloadable official documents are stored beside this file under docs/sources/ and are git-ignored by extension, exactly as docs/study/sources/*.pdf already is. The DIGEST is committed here; the bytes are not, because this repository is public and the instruments are served by their own publishers.
conventions.field_vocabulary: source_id, source_class, provider, original_url, sha256, bytes and verification_status follow docs/study/historical_source_layer.json (schema miw.study.historical_source_layer.v1) so the two layers read alike.
conventions.access_discipline: Authentication, access controls, robots restrictions and publisher restrictions are never bypassed. Where bytes cannot lawfully or technically be obtained the entry is ACCESS_LIMITED and preserves metadata, the official URL, the publisher announcement and the specific verified claims - never a pretence that the document was archived.
conventions.history: A superseded entry is retained and marked, never overwritten. New official truth wins for production; the old record stays as evidence of what was true when.

currentness_states.CURRENT_VERIFIED: Verified against the issuer's own most recent statement at checked_on.
currentness_states.CURRENT_BUT_RECHECK_ON_EVENT: Believed current, but a named event could change it before any date-based review would.
currentness_states.HISTORICAL_SUPERSEDED: A later version exists. Retained as predecessor evidence; must not be used as current truth.
currentness_states.FUTURE_ADOPTED_NOT_EFFECTIVE: Adopted with a known effective date still ahead; does not govern sittings before it.
currentness_states.ACCESS_LIMITED: Identity and issuer verified, but the document's own bytes could not lawfully or technically be retrieved. Claims are limited to what the publisher has stated publicly.
currentness_states.CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED: Not established. Barred from candidate-facing use.

sources.edition: The resolution as adopted 23 May 2024, held in full; plus IMO's January 2026 publication supplement to the 1991 Edition (sales number I240E), which carries the same amendment INCOMPLETELY
sources.issuing_authority: International Maritime Organization
sources.issuing_authority_note: IMO itself, as publisher of the Code and of its own supplement. Tier 1 - this is not a class-society or P&I restatement.
sources.source_type: official publication supplement carrying an adopted MSC resolution
sources.authority_rank: Mandatory. The Grain Code is given force by SOLAS chapter VI, part C, regulation 9; MSC.552(108) amends the Code itself.
sources.access_note: TWO IMO FILES ARE HELD AND THEY DO NOT AGREE. The AUTHORITY is the resolution itself (6 pages, full text layer, operative clauses and complete annex), retrieved from IMO's resolutions index. The companion is IMO's January 2026 publication supplement (132,651 bytes, sha256 2201d471db0ebac7f8c4f23ad82c0a6f6e141c57810d37190e513a10b1fe1432), which is INCOMPLETE in two ways: it OMITS annex item 6 (the A 12.3.3 cross-reference repair) and carries NO operative clauses at all. This registry entry originally cited the supplement alone; the resolution was obtained after an independent reviewer challenged the amendment list, and the discrepancy is the reason the entry now names the resolution as authority. A supplement to a sales publication is an editorial aid, not the instrument. Both files are filed in the shared desktop-team corpus at 03-imo-instruments/Grain-Code/ with the discrepancy recorded in its INSTRUMENT_LOG.md.
sources.publication_date_note: Supplement dated January 2026; the resolution it carries was adopted 23 May 2024.
sources.effective_date_note: MSC.552(108) entered into force 1 January 2026 and applies to both new and existing ships - there is no newbuilding-only limb.
sources.supersedes_note: Amends the 1991 Edition; it does not replace the Code.
sources.checked_how: Asked the publisher-anchored question rather than the supersession question: what is the most recent Grain Code amendment IMO itself publishes? IMO's current supplement to the 1991 Edition is the January 2026 one and its whole content is MSC.552(108). Independently re-checked against MSC 109, MSC 110 and MSC 111 outcomes - MSC 111 (13-22 May 2026) adopted the MASS Code, SOLAS IV/V amendments, the ESP Code and IMDG 43-26, and no Grain Code amendment.
sources.revalidation_note: Not yet confirmed against the official IMO depositary/status list, which is the stronger check this corpus uses elsewhere. Logged as RQ-G02 in the shared corpus review queue.
verified_claims: Adopted by MSC at its 108th session by resolution MSC.552(108) on 23 May 2024, under SOLAS article VIII(b)(iv); deemed accepted 1 July 2025 under article VIII(b)(vi)(2)(bb); in force 1 January 2026 under article VIII(b)(vii)(2).
The resolution contains NO application clause, so it binds new and existing ships alike. This can only be established from the resolution - the supplement carries no operative clauses.
The Grain Code was adopted by resolution MSC.23(59) and is mandatory under SOLAS chapter VI; the amendment procedure is article VIII(b) read with regulation VI/8.1.

New definition A 2.8: "specially suitable compartment, partly filled in way of the hatch opening, with ends untrimmed" - not filled to the maximum extent in way of the hatch opening but filled to a level equal with or above the bottom edge of the hatch end beams, and not trimmed outside the periphery of the hatch opening by A 10.4.
New A 10.4 permits the grain outside the hatch periphery to lie at its natural angle of repose and allows dispensation from trimming the ends.
A 10.7 (ex 10.6) replaced: only the free surface in way of the hatch opening need be level in such a compartment.

New B 1.1.5: surface assumed to slope in all directions at 30 degrees from the lower edge of the hatch end beam; if feeding holes per table B 1-2 are provided and the free surface in way of the hatch opening is above them, from the mean line on the hatch end beam as shown in figure B-1.
B 1.5 replaced: total heeling moment = 1.12 x calculated transverse heeling moment, now covering the new category as well as partly filled compartments.
New Part B section 4: B 2 provisions for filled-and-trimmed compartments apply, except that after shifting the surfaces are assumed at 25 degrees to the horizontal.

Sixteen numbered annex items in total. Consequential cross-reference and renumbering changes in A 10.3.1, A 10.10.3, A 12.3.3 (annex item 6, under heading 12 Divisions loaded on both sides - PRESENT IN THE RESOLUTION AND ABSENT FROM THE SUPPLEMENT), A 14.1, B 1.2, B 2.6, B 2.8, B 2.9, B 3.1 and renumbered B 5.
claims_NOT_established: That MSC.552(108) requires the approved grain loading manual or Document of Authorization to be updated. This is widely and correctly stated as PRACTICAL GUIDANCE by class societies and P&I clubs (LR class news 09/25, Britannia, BIMCO, NorthStandard) and follows from the ship only being loadable to a condition its approved booklet covers - but it is NOT in the amendment text and must not be attributed to the resolution.
Anything about the Grain Code outside this amendment delta. The 1991 base publication is NOT held (RQ-G01 in the shared corpus review queue).

verified_claims: A 3.1: 'A document of authorization shall be issued for every ship loaded in accordance with the regulations of this Code either by the Administration or an organization recognized by it or by a Contracting Government on behalf of the Administration. It shall be accepted as evidence that the ship is capable of complying with the requirements of these regulations.'
A 3.2: 'The document shall accompany or be incorporated into the grain loading manual provided to enable the master to meet the requirements of A 7. The manual shall meet the requirements of A 6.3.'

sources.title: National Maritime Decarbonisation Policy Framework 2026 (draft)
sources.edition: Draft dated 3 July 2026, published on DGMA's Maritime INDIA @ Net Zero page
sources.issuing_authority: Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
sources.issuing_authority_note: DGMA is the competent maritime authority; the page also carries the Draft National Green Shipping Policy version 6 (4 May 2026) and eight pillar implementation roadmaps.
sources.authority_rank: DRAFT. Authoritative as to what the competent authority PROPOSES; it is NOT law, NOT notified policy, and creates no obligation. This distinction is load-bearing for any candidate-facing use.
sources.access_note: 104 pages, full text layer. WARNING: the document is internally inconsistent in places - see claims_NOT_established. Read its deployment-status sections (Part I section 4 onward, and the "what is deployed or actively underway as of mid-2026" chapter) before relying on any narrative summary earlier in it.
sources.publication_date_note: The most recent document on DGMA's Maritime INDIA @ Net Zero page as at 31 August 2026.
sources.effective_date_note: None - it is a draft framework. Recording 'no effective date' is the point, not an omission.
sources.supersedes_note: It does not supersede Harit Sagar, the Green Tug Transition Programme, MIV-2030 or MAKV-2047; it is the policy spine intended to connect them.
sources.checked_how: Asked what DGMA has published MOST RECENTLY on Indian maritime decarbonisation, rather than checking a known programme list. That is what surfaced the National Green Shipping Policy and this framework, neither of which appeared in the earlier programme-by-programme currency record.
sources.revalidation_note: A DRAFT at version 6 is by definition moving. Re-check the DGMA page before any currentness-sensitive use, and expect a notified policy to replace this framing. When re-reading, go to the deployment-status chapters, not the narrative ones.
verified_claims: The framework is built on eight pillars: Green Shipbuilding and Retrofits; Green Ports; Green Ship Recycling; Green Finance; Green Skill; Alternate Fuels; Green Technology; Pollution Prevention / Waste Management.
The Draft National Green Shipping Policy is at version 6 dated 4 May 2026 and is structured around seven pillars - the framework's eight add Pollution Prevention.

Maritime INDIA @ Net Zero is described as a multi-ministerial platform to translate the National Green Shipping Policy into coordinated national action; a workshop was held on 14-15 January 2026 at the India Habitat Centre with 312 participants.

Harit Sagar Green Port Guidelines were issued by MoPSW in 2023 and require, among other things, all major ports to achieve 60% renewable electricity consumption by 2030, shore power connectivity at major ports on specified timelines, ISO 14001 certification, and greenhouse-gas inventories with carbon emissions tracked per tonne of cargo handled.
Pilot ports identified for green hydrogen and ammonia bunkering infrastructure: JNPT, Kandla, Visakhapatnam, Paradip, Kochi and Chennai.

The Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme is extended to 31 March 2036 with a corpus of Rs 24,736 crore; a Shipbuilding Development Scheme with an outlay of Rs 19,989 crore is PROPOSED; the capacity target is 4.5 million Gross Tonnage annually.
India's port decarbonisation is guided by Harit Sagar carbon accounting rather than by a port equivalent of the MARPOL Annex VI CII, which applies to ships of 5,000 GT and above.

The Green Tug Transition Programme was LAUNCHED IN OCTOBER 2024 and is described as India's most advanced vessel-level decarbonisation initiative. PHASE 1 COVERS FOUR PILOT PORTS - Deendayal, JNPA, Paradip and V.O. Chidambaranar - with two green tugs to be procured or chartered at each, and work orders placed at all four. Deendayal has completed tender float and contract award; VOCPA, JNPA, PPA, NMPA and VPA have issued Notices Inviting Tender. Cochin (KPL) is planning green tug procurement only after its current diesel tug contract expires in August 2027 - it is NOT a Phase 1 port. India's first all-electric tug, built by Atreya Shipyard for Deendayal with Kongsberg permanent-magnet propulsion, was expected by late 2026. About 100 green tugs are in the procurement pipeline at approximately Rs 12,000 crore.

Renewable energy was 15.48% of total electricity consumption across Indian major ports as of 2023-24; Deendayal Port Authority is at 69.41% and Mumbai Port Authority at 87.22%, both already past the 60% target, and nine major ports are on track for 2030.

A Cabinet-approved allocation of Rs 69,725 crore spans four schemes: SBFAS Rs 24,736 crore, Maritime Development Fund Rs 25,000 crore (Maritime Investment Fund Rs 20,000 cr + Interest Incentivisation Fund Rs 5,000 cr), Shipbuilding Development Scheme Rs 19,989 crore, and legal / policy / process reforms as a structural enabler. The framework states that "none of these allocations are currently green-labelled, green-conditioned, or subject to environmental performance criteria" and that no maritime-specific green finance taxonomy exists.

Harit Sagar requires an annual port-level GHG inventory and reduction targets "aligned with the IMO Port Carbon Intensity Indicator (PCII) framework"; a Port CII concept therefore EXISTS, while Indian port performance is measured as carbon per tonne of cargo handled against Environmental Performance Indicators.
The framework proposes mandatory sustainable-biofuel blending for domestic coastal vessels commencing 2027, with ISCC or RSB certification and a Proof of Sustainability document.
claims_NOT_established: That the National Green Shipping Policy or this framework has been NOTIFIED or adopted. Both are drafts as at 31 August 2026.

The "23% renewable energy use at ports" figure carried by the earlier August currency record. DGMA's own framework states 60% renewable electricity at major ports by 2030 under Harit Sagar, against a 15.48% baseline. The 23% figure was not located in any DGMA document read here and is not used.
That any Green Tug Transition Programme tug is in service.

THE DOCUMENT CONTRADICTS ITSELF AND MIW DOES NOT PICK A SIDE. (1) On the GTTP pilot ports: its narrative chapter says "pilot deployments at JNPT and Kochi", its deployment-status chapter says Phase 1 is Deendayal, JNPA, Paradip and V.O. Chidambaranar with Cochin waiting until 2027. The status chapter is the one that describes reality and is what MIW uses; the first version of the card used the narrative chapter and was WRONG, caught by independent review. (2) On the GTTP end date: one section says at least 30% green tugs at all major ports by 2030 with full transition by 2036, another says 50 green tugs by 2030 and full fleet transition by 2047.

Time between overhauls lengthened up to 18,000 running hours.
Hydrocarbon and carbon monoxide emissions significantly reduced - stated qualitatively, with NO percentage.

Applicable engine list includes medium-size RT-flex50 B/D, RT-flex58T/B/D/E, RT-flex60C/CB, RT-flex68B/D Tier2, RT-flex82C Tier1 and large-size RT-flex82C Tier2, RT-flex82T, RT-flex84T-D Tier2, RTA96C, RT-flex96C-B with and without WHR.

Applicability to MAN B&W engines. The engine list is Wartsila 2-stroke only.
That the family is RT-flex only - RTA96C is on the maker's own list, which corrects the internal note that said otherwise.
